_readme: Doctrine A — the shared corpus. THE SPLIT IS ONE RULE IN TWO LANGUAGES.
the same law written twice, because one runs on the prelim path (Python)
and one runs on the SiteX path (TypeScript). Two implementations of a rule
drift; that is not a risk, it is a schedule.
So neither implementation is the authority — THIS FILE is. Both test
suites read it and assert the same split on every case. A change to one
side that the other does not make fails in the language that did not
change, which is the only failure mode that catches a one-sided edit.
A marker-list mirror test also pins the patterns character-for-character.
That guards the spelling. This corpus guards the property. Both are here
because a pin that guards a spelling does not guard a property.
`parties: null` means: nothing may be offered as a fact from this string.
`absent: true` means the splitter returns nothing at all (U0).

cases.input: JOHN A. DOE AND JANE B. DOE, HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.verbatim: JOHN A. DOE AND JANE B. DOE, HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.parties: JOHN A. DOE AND JANE B. DOE
cases.characterization: HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.why: H1 §2.2's own example. Two names, one characterization, one split.
A bare name is a fact, whole. The common case, and it must not be disturbed.
Marital status is a characterization even when it names no tenancy.

cases.input: JOHN DOE AND JANE DOE, HUSBAND AND WIFE, AS COMMUNITY PROPERTY WITH RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP
cases.verbatim: JOHN DOE AND JANE DOE, HUSBAND AND WIFE, AS COMMUNITY PROPERTY WITH RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP
cases.characterization: HUSBAND AND WIFE, AS COMMUNITY PROPERTY WITH RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP
cases.why: Two adjacent markers separated by nothing but punctuation are ONE characterization, not an ambiguity.

cases.input: ROBERT SMITH AND LINDA SMITH, TRUSTEES OF THE SMITH FAMILY TRUST DATED JANUARY 5, 2011
cases.verbatim: ROBERT SMITH AND LINDA SMITH, TRUSTEES OF THE SMITH FAMILY TRUST DATED JANUARY 5, 2011
cases.characterization: TRUSTEES OF THE SMITH FAMILY TRUST DATED JANUARY 5, 2011
cases.why: The trust's name is a fact, but it arrives welded to a CAPACITY. The whole tail is proposed rather than half of it silently promoted.
An entity's NAME includes its suffix. Stripping 'LLC' would corrupt the fact — the marker requires the article ('a California limited liability company'), which is the recital, not the name.

cases.input: ACME HOLDINGS, LLC, A CALIFORNIA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY
cases.verbatim: ACME HOLDINGS, LLC, A CALIFORNIA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY
cases.why: The entity recital is the characterization; the name keeps its suffix.

cases.input: DOE JOHN A & DOE JANE B
cases.verbatim: DOE JOHN A & DOE JANE B
cases.parties: DOE JOHN A & DOE JANE B
cases.why: County-record surname-first format. Ugly, but entirely fact — and it must not be mistaken for mixed content.

cases.input: HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.verbatim: HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.characterization: HUSBAND AND WIFE AS JOINT TENANTS
cases.why: A characterization with no name in front of it. There is no fact to offer, and inventing one from the characterization would be exactly backwards.

cases.input: JOHN DOE, AN UNMARRIED MAN AND MARY ROE, A SINGLE WOMAN, AS TENANTS IN COMMON
cases.verbatim: JOHN DOE, AN UNMARRIED MAN AND MARY ROE, A SINGLE WOMAN, AS TENANTS IN COMMON
cases.why: THE CASE THAT MATTERS. Splitting at the first marker would put MARY ROE inside the characterization and drop a real owner out of the fact position — a missing grantor is worse than an unsplit string. A name between two markers means we cannot split confidently, so we do not.

cases.input: JOHN DOE, A MARRIED MAN, AS HIS SOLE AND SEPARATE PROPERTY
cases.verbatim: JOHN DOE, A MARRIED MAN, AS HIS SOLE AND SEPARATE PROPERTY
cases.characterization: A MARRIED MAN, AS HIS SOLE AND SEPARATE PROPERTY
cases.why: Two markers, no name between them — one characterization.

cases.input: John Doe and Jane Doe, husband and wife as joint tenants
cases.verbatim: John Doe and Jane Doe, husband and wife as joint tenants
cases.characterization: husband and wife as joint tenants
cases.why: Not every source shouts. The split is case-insensitive; the OUTPUT keeps the source's casing, because a verbatim that has been re-cased is not a verbatim.

A PDF text layer wraps mid-line. The wrap is layout, not content, so runs of whitespace normalise to one space before anything is matched — otherwise the marker straddles a newline and is never found.
Edge whitespace and a dangling separator are trimmed. A trailing comma is punctuation left over from the line above it, not part of anyone's name.
U0 — absence is not a candidate. An empty string produces NOTHING, not an empty candidate for the officer to confirm.
